answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the dawn hash is checked against the jetty checkpoint at intake, the pulse audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 428 identities multiplies that fee by 590 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
